title: Ultrafast Proton-Induced Collective Dynamics Regulated by Water-Mediated Hydrogen-Bond Networks in Liquids
authors: Xiaokun Liu, Bozhu Chen, Yizhu Zhang, Jiyu Xu, Meng Li, Yanjun Gao, Ji Qi, Yuqian Yang, Wennan Wang, Sheng Meng, Yuhai Jiang
abstract: Photoinduced proton dynamics in liquids couple molecular reactions to nonequilibrium charge transport, yet the role of alkyl C-H sites as proton sources remains poorly understood. Combining optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy with real-time time-dependent density-functional-theory simulations, we investigate ultrafast proton dynamics following strong-field ionization of liquid ethanol and hydroxyl-free ethyl acetate. Isotope-substitution and control experiments support the identification of alkyl C-H groups as the proton source. The released protons induce quasi-free-electron localization on a timescale of hundreds of femtoseconds, manifested as a characteristic V-shaped transient in terahertz absorption. In ethanol-water mixtures, trace water enhances hydrogen-bond-network connectivity and facilitates proton transfer to ethanol O-H sites, suppressing the transient absorption dip. These findings identify photoactivated C-H sites as proton sources in liquids and reveal how hydrogen-bond networks regulate the ensuing proton and electron dynamics, linking local bond cleavage to the ultrafast charge response of the surrounding liquid.
summary: This paper uses combined THz spectroscopy and advanced simulations to track proton dynamics in liquid organic solvents. It establishes that photoionization triggers proton release from C-H bonds, which creates a measurable transient electronic signature. Crucially, it demonstrates that the surrounding hydrogen-bond network actively regulates this process by scavenging free protons, linking local chemistry to collective electronic behavior.
main_problem: The study investigates the ultrafast dynamics of protons following photoexcitation in liquids, specifically determining the role of alkyl C-H sites as proton donors and how hydrogen-bond networks regulate the subsequent proton and electron transport.
main_result: The research identifies photoactivated C-H sites as the primary proton sources, evidenced by a characteristic V-shaped transient in THz absorption, and shows that water-mediated hydrogen-bond networks suppress this transient by facilitating proton recombination.
method: The work combines experimental Optical-Pump Terahertz-Probe (OPTP) spectroscopy with real-time time-dependent density-functional-theory (rt-TDDFT) simulations.
model_or_system: The system involves liquid ethanol, ethyl acetate, and their mixtures with water, focusing on the dynamics of proton transfer and quasi-free electron localization in these condensed phases.
key_observables: Transient change in THz absorption ($\Delta E/E$), quasi-free electron localization (V-shaped transient), and proton transfer rates.
important_parameters: Ultrafast timescales (hundreds of femtoseconds), and the concentration of water in the liquid mixture.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the THz signal is governed by liquid conductivity dynamics ($\Delta\sigma \propto \Delta n$) and that C-H cleavage is the dominant proton source under the studied conditions.
figures_summary: Figures show OPTP results for pure water and ethanol, illustrating the V-shaped dip attributed to C-H cleavage, and how this dip attenuates in ethanol-water mixtures as water content increases.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the problem of proton dynamics, presents OPTP and rt-TDDFT results comparing pure liquids (ethanol, water) and mixtures, confirms C-H origin via control experiments, and concludes by linking local bond cleavage to collective charge response.
why_interesting: The coupling between local bond cleavage (C-H activation) and the collective, ultrafast charge response of the solvent (THz signal) is a key topic in non-equilibrium quantum dynamics, highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems.

For 0 < τ < 500 fs, the rapid increase in |∆E(τ)/E| indicates a rapid increase in the density of quasi-free electrons in the liquid due to pho- toionization.
